item.title: ‘Grand Theft Auto VI’ Debut Spurs Livestream Influencer Marathons
item.description: Take-Two Interactive's Rockstar Games released Grand Theft Auto VI, triggering an unprecedented traffic surge on Twitch with 3.3 million concurrent viewers. Financial models project the title to surpass $3 billion in revenue within its initial months based on current pre-order demand and community engagement.

item.title: Temu Owner Reports Flat Profit, Revenue as Challenges Continue
item.description: PDD Holdings reported a 0.7% YoY net profit increase to 29.54 billion yuan with flat revenue. The company faces significant headwinds as its overseas platform, Temu, encounters severe scrutiny from the European Commission over content moderation and illegal product sanctions, compounded by cooling domestic consumer demand.

item.title: OpenAI's own researchers now say they value their AI tools more than nearly half their colleagues
item.description: OpenAI's internal report reveals a massive surge in the use of autonomous agents for R&D, with theoretical compute costs now exceeding base researcher salaries at $2,400 per person per day. While agents show a 79% success rate in routine monitoring, they remain significantly constrained in complex engineering and scaffolding tasks.

item.title: I let Apple’s always-listening AI summarize my life for two weeks

item.title: IEA Sees Data Center Boom Pushing Power Grids to the Limit
item.description: The IEA's World Energy Outlook 2026 projects that AI-driven data center demand could double electricity consumption to 1,000 TWh by 2030. Supply chain constraints for critical equipment and grid expansion speeds are emerging as the primary bottlenecks for scaling AI infrastructure.

item.title: Canva adds an AI ‘off’ button
item.description: Canva has introduced an 'off' switch for generative AI features, allowing users to disable tools like Magic Expand and its chatbot while retaining non-generative utilities like background removal. This move responds to user frustration over AI proliferation and introduces filters to limit AI-generated content in search results.

item.title: Germany, Austria Propose Trump-Style Takeover of TikTok’s EU Ops
item.description: German Media Minister Wolfram Weimer and Austrian Digital Secretary Alexander Pröll have proposed moving TikTok's European operations under European ownership. The initiative aims to mitigate data security concerns related to its Chinese parent company, ByteDance, mirroring recent forced-divestiture models seen in the US.

item.title: A human liver has been kept alive outside the body for a record seven weeks
item.description: Researchers in Australia claim they’ve kept a human liver alive, on life support, outside the body for seven weeks, opening up speculative new possibilities in biomedical engineering. The feat, whose details are pending publication, was carried out in Sydney after a team led by surgeon and inventor Carlo Pulitano connected a donated liver to a system of automated pumps and sensors that fed the organ nutrients, supplied it with blood, and whisked away waste. item.title: Google is forcing Android app developers to properly support foldables
item.description: Now that Apple’s foldable is here, Google wants to make sure apps on Android foldables are a good experience. Starting in April 2027, Google is going to require Android developers to make sure their apps have a baseline level of support for foldables. If they don’t, developers risk not being able to publish or update their apps or have reduced visibility for their apps on Google Play. item.description: Snapchat announced on Wednesday that it’s giving Lens creators the ability to build Lenses using the AI coding assistants they already use, like Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex. Snapchat Lenses, which are a core part of the social network’s platform, are AR effects that let users alter their appearance, add digital objects to their surroundings, or interact with animated experiences through the camera. item.title: Korea becomes world's 4th country to reach $1 tril. in annual exports
item.description: The South Korean Ministry of Trade, Industry and Resources announced that the nation's annual exports hit $1 trillion for the first time, fueled by robust demand for semiconductors and data center infrastructure driven by global AI investment. While full-year projections reach $1.17 trillion, officials warned that potential slowdowns in AI spending, chip price volatility, and trade barriers remain key risks to future momentum.

item.title: European Retail Traders Snag $1.1 Billion of Anthropic IPO Stock
item.description: AI lab Anthropic PBC raised $1.1 billion from retail investors in the UK and continental Europe as part of a record-breaking $107.3 billion initial public offering. Despite market concerns regarding the pace of AI spending and market volatility, the company successfully priced its IPO above the marketed range.

item.title: TSMC and Samsung suspend some chip shipments to Chinese customers
item.description: TSMC and Samsung Electronics have suspended shipments of certain advanced processors to Chinese customers following new export control rules from the US Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS). The updated regulations remove exemptions previously used to bypass AI-related export restrictions, mandating that foundries must obtain specific US government licenses for advanced manufacturing orders, significantly impacting Chinese AI and consumer electronics companies.

item.title: OCR models now digitize a million pages for under $130 as costs drop fivefold in 18 months
item.description: Research from Hugging Face indicates that the cost of large-scale document OCR has dropped fivefold over the past 18 months, driven by lightweight model architectures and improved GPU rental efficiencies. Processing one million pages now costs between $65 and $130 in GPU compute, with newer models achieving parity in accuracy compared to older, more expensive counterparts.

item.title: A profile of Netflix's new Chief Content Officer Peter Rice, a former Fox and Disney executive, as sources say he may focus on revamping its film strategy (Alex Weprin/The Hollywood Reporter)
item.description: Netflix co-CEO Ted Sarandos has appointed former Disney Entertainment Chairman and Fox executive Peter Rice as the new Chief Content Officer, succeeding Bela Bajaria to overhaul the streamer's content strategy. With his proven track record in scaling FX and Hulu, Rice is tasked with shifting Netflix’s output from quantity-driven models toward a mix of commercial viability and high-end prestige productions.

item.title: The Anti-A.I. Campus Movement Is Growing
item.description: University students and faculty globally are protesting the integration of generative AI through petitions, religious exemption filings, and manifestos. The movement seeks to curtail institutional partnerships with AI vendors like OpenAI and Google, citing concerns over the erosion of critical thinking and the intrinsic value of human-centric education.

item.title: US companies turn to robots to ease labour shortage crisis
item.description: North American manufacturers are accelerating robot adoption to mitigate severe labor shortages, with Q3 2026 orders reaching 11,000 units, a 25% year-on-year increase. Notably, orders for collaborative robots (cobots) surged by 56%, serving as a critical lever for firms to scale output amid persistent workforce limitations.

item.title: Google Ruth Porat Pledges Data Center Local Support Amid Backlash
item.description: Alphabet and Google President Ruth Porat announced a $15 billion investment in data center infrastructure in Missouri. The central project, 'Project Spade' in Montgomery County, targets a 1.2GW capacity. To address energy needs, Google is partnering with utility providers Ameren and Evergy to secure 500MW of additional grid capacity while utilizing a Capacity Commitment Framework (CCF) to protect local rate payers.

item.title: Anthropic retail investors face squeeze in blockbuster IPO
item.description: Anthropic aims to allocate approximately 20% of its IPO to individual investors, yet the offering has been heavily oversubscribed by institutional demand managed by JPMorgan. Despite efforts through brokers like Robinhood and Fidelity, the significant oversubscription is expected to compress the final retail allocation below the initial 20% target.
